C0.quote: agents with single-peaked preferences can participate in a costly voting procedure

C1.loc: Section 3, Theorem 1; Section 2, Observation; Section 4, Corollary 1
C1.quote: There does not exist an anonymous and strategy-proof voting mechanism
C1.note: Main results are equilibrium characterisations. The Observation (which generalized medians satisfy responsiveness) and Corollary 1 (incompatibility of properties) are axiomatic.

C2.1.value: profile of preferences; votes; reported peak
C2.1.quote: maps every profile of preferences of the agents in K

C2.2.quote: F k only depends on the individual peaks
C2.2.note: Inputs are single-peaked ordinal preference relations over [0,1]; strategy-proof rules use only reported peaks, i.e. points in [0,1].

C2.3.quote: characterized by a single-peaked (ordinal) preference relation
C2.3.note: Agents also have preferences over outcome-participation pairs and participation costs.

C2.4.quote: we cannot assume that the reported peaks coincide with the true peaks
C2.4.note: Reported peaks are given separate notation from true peaks pi.

C3.1.quote: assume that all participants who actually cast a vote submit their true peak
C3.1.note: Theorem 1 assumes truthful votes; the symmetric median analysis (Theorem 2) has non-truthful reporting.

C3.2.quote: We will therefore assume that all participants who actually cast a vote

C3.3.quote: voting truthfully is the unique (weakly) dominant strategy for every participant
C3.3.note: Also justified by refinements (perfectness, strong equilibrium).

C4.1.note: Input format coded OTH (single-peaked preferences/peaks), so the applicability condition is not met.

C5.1.quote: the corresponding voting mechanism is efficient
C5.1.note: Efficiency is used in the Observation and in the proof of Theorem 1.

C5.2.loc: Section 2 Observation; Section 4, Corollary 1 and discussion
C5.2.quote: yields the median peak for all distributions of individual peaks
C5.2.note: Evaluation is against true peaks, which the paper notates separately from reported peaks (C2.4 = DIST).

VOT.quote_behav: Agents take two decisions: whether or not to participate
VOT.quote_info: Our analysis is embedded in a simple voting model with complete information.
VOT.note: Voters choose participation strategically. Under strategy-proof rules their vote is their dominant (truthful) strategy.

DES.note: Mechanisms are characterised by properties; the designer's choice or objective is not modelled.

C8.1.quote: we assume that in the second stage a strong Nash equilibrium is played
C8.1.note: OTH: (trembling-hand) perfect equilibrium, used in Theorem 1a.

C8.2.quote: The sequential voting game has a unique subgame perfect equilibrium

Strategy-proofness is desirable because without it the social outcome cannot
our model applies to decisions in small committees

C9.2.quote: If individual utilities can be measured by objective distance
C9.2.note: The welfare claim states its utility assumption. The committee claim relies on complete information, which is stated and defended (p.3). Truthfulness is stated via strategy-proofness.

C1.reason: The Observation and Corollary 1 are axiomatic results about which rules satisfy which properties, so AX belongs in the types alongside EQ and SB.

C5.2.reason: INPUT-STATED requires C2.4 in {IDJ, IDS}, but here C2.4 is DIST and outcomes are judged against true peaks, so HELD fits.
